documents.title: Guidance on the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: Provost-office guidance for instructors. It leaves AI permissions to each instructor and asks for syllabus statements covering assessed and non-assessed work, detection and consequences. It also covers AI in grading, distrust of detectors, copyright uploads and FERPA.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Authorization is determined at the course level by the instructor' and that instructors 'should determine and inform students when the use of AI is authorized or unauthorized'; it sets no university-wide permission or ban, so it delegates.

units.why: This states the purpose and scope of the page ('to provide reasonably thorough, but also accessible and brief, guidance to support the AI approaches and practices of instructors'), an institution-level framing preamble, so P56, informs.

units.fit_note: Also says student-facing guidance will be written; P54 only covers revisiting and feedback. Promises a separate student-facing guidance document, not just revision of this one.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Use (VII.A.5)
documents.summary: An IT policy issued November 2025 on GenAI and LLM use across the university. It authorizes approved tools, restricts sensitive data, bars AI as the sole basis for personnel, award or disciplinary decisions, and requires incident reporting and training. Classroom use is deferred to the provost guidelines.
documents.stance_why: Policy VII.A.5 says 'The responsible use of approved AI tools and technologies is authorized subject to the following requirements', which allows AI with conditions on data, approved tools and review; classroom decisions are left to 'Provost guidelines'. Resolution: B coded delegates because classroom use is passed to 'Provost guidelines'; A coded permit. The document itself authorizes AI use, with conditions, across the university, and only the classroom question is deferred, so permit is kept.

units.frag_start: Usage authorization review by the Data
units.fit_note: Use-case review by the Data Ethics Committee rather than review of the tool itself.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded 'Usage authorization review by the Data Ethics Committee is initiated by completion of a Data Ethics Committee Use Case Review.' A skipped it. Source describes the use-case review procedure that a tool needs before use, a real requirement; kept as P50 (vetted tools) rather than B's P65 because it reviews a use case, not vendor agreements.

units.why: 'the user(s) must immediately report the incident' when non-public data is uploaded to an unapproved AI tool is a duty to report data exposure, P71.
units.anchor: the user(s) must immediately report the incident
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B neutral. Source: 'the user(s) must immediately report the incident'. It is an incident-reporting duty and takes no position on AI use: neutral.

units.why: 'Purdue University supports responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies' gives the rationale for allowing AI, P56.
units.anchor: Purdue University supports responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies
units.fit_note: Rationale for permitting AI rather than a rule.
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (institution-wide framework), B coded P02 (permit or encourage by default). Source: 'Purdue University supports responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies.' It welcomes AI use, which is P02, and unit_stance encourage; it does not itself set a framework.

units.why: Warns that information entered into AI tools without an agreement 'may become the property of the tool provider and be used in training', a data and IP risk, P50.
units.anchor: may become the property of the tool provider and be used in training its services

units.why: 'Responsible use of AI is essential to maintaining academic integrity, data security and institutional standards' states why the policy exists, P56.
units.anchor: Responsible use of AI is essential to maintaining academic integrity, data security and institutional standards.

units.why: The policy applies to 'All Purdue persons, departments, units, contractors, consultants and campuses using AI' and has 'no exclusions', which sets scope, P56.
units.anchor: All Purdue persons, departments, units, contractors, consultants and campuses using AI.

units.why: Faculty, staff, students and others must 'use AI in compliance with this policy', a general compliance duty, P77.
units.anchor: Use AI in compliance with this policy.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B general. Source: 'Use AI in compliance with this policy.' The duty applies while using AI: during-work.

units.why: Users must 'complete applicable training on appropriate use of AI as required by Purdue IT', a training mandate, P70.
units.anchor: Complete applicable training on appropriate use of AI as required by Purdue IT.

units.why: The CISO is told to 'oversee ongoing implementation of this policy', assigning ownership; no type covers role assignment for maintaining a policy, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Oversee ongoing implementation of this policy.
units.uncovered_note: Names the CISO as responsible for overseeing implementation of the AI use policy.
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED, B coded P76. Source: the CISO must 'Oversee ongoing implementation of this policy.' It assigns responsibility for the policy's implementation, which no type captures; kept UNCOVERED, grouped with A21 and A22 (responsibility assignments for implementing, monitoring and excepting this policy).

units.why: Purdue Systems Security must 'implement monitoring to identify and remediate policy violations', an institutional monitoring duty for IT misuse; no type fits since it is not coursework detection, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Implement monitoring to identify and remediate policy violations.
units.uncovered_note: IT security staff monitor to identify and remediate violations of the AI use policy. (B: IT security office monitors for violations of the AI use policy and remediates them.)
units.resolution_why: Both coders marked UNCOVERED. Source: Purdue Systems Security must 'Implement monitoring to identify and remediate policy violations.' It assigns monitoring and remediation of AI-policy violations to IT security; no type covers that.

units.why: Systems Security must 'process policy exceptions', an exception procedure for the AI policy that fits no listed type, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Process policy exceptions.
units.uncovered_note: A process exists to grant exceptions to the AI use policy.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded 'Process policy exceptions.' B skipped it. Source assigns Purdue Systems Security the exceptions process, a distinct responsibility; kept UNCOVERED.

units.why: The Data Ethics Committee must 'ensure appropriate legal agreements are in place with third-party AI tools', a review of vendor agreements, P65.
units.anchor: Ensure appropriate legal agreements are in place with third-party AI tools

units.why: Committee must 'ensure any approved AI tool put into use follows Purdue's AI Guiding Principles', pointing to an institutional principles framework, P56.
units.anchor: Ensure any approved AI tool put into use follows Purdue's AI Guiding Principles.
units.fit_note: Refers to separate AI Guiding Principles whose content is not in this text.

units.why: Committee will 'provide recommendations on policy changes regarding the use of AI', a mechanism for revising the policy, P54.
units.anchor: Provide recommendations on policy changes regarding the use of AI at Purdue.

units.why: Committee must 'consider potential reputational harm from the implementation of Purdue-facing AI tools', an operational review concern about public-facing AI, P76.
units.anchor: Consider potential reputational harm from the implementation of Purdue-facing AI tools.
units.fit_note: Asks committee to weigh reputational harm to the university, not data or legal risk.
units.resolution_why: A coded P76, B coded UNCOVERED. Source: the Data Ethics Committee must 'Consider potential reputational harm from the implementation of Purdue-facing AI tools.' It sets a consideration governing implementation of operational AI tools, which fits P76 (govern administrative and operational AI use) partly.

units.why: Committee will 'review and approve enterprise-level training modules on appropriate use of AI', training provided to the community, P70.
units.anchor: Review and approve enterprise-level training modules on appropriate use of AI.

units.why: The history says the policy was 'reviewed, no changes' in 2026, evidence of a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: Policy reviewed, no changes.

notes: Only the two included university-layer documents were coded; school/computing none-found, course deferred. VII.A.5 is an IT/data policy and says little about coursework. The CTL page mentions a Spring 2024 town hall, so parts of it may predate its August 2025 modification. B's note: topic codes taken from tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md. One A-only unit (Spring 2024 town hall invitation on the CTL page) was dropped as an event notice, not a policy.
